blocks.text: KING OF EGYPT (NOT NAMED IN SCRIPTURE) · EGYPT
Pharaoh of Joseph's day. The king who raised Joseph from the prison to rule Egypt.
REIGNEDi

Not given Scripture gives no length of reign. "Pharaoh" raised Joseph at thirty and was still the title of the king who let Joseph bury Jacob, about twenty-six years later (Gen 41:46; 45:6; 47:28; 50:6).

WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
He dreamed of seven fat and seven lean kine, and of full and thin ears, and none of the magicians or wise men of Egypt could interpret it. Genesis 41:1–8
Joseph told him: "God hath shewed Pharaoh what he is about to do." Genesis 41:25
He asked his servants, "Can we find such a one as this is, a man in whom the Spirit of God is?" Genesis 41:38
He set Joseph over all Egypt: "only in the throne will I be greater than thou." Genesis 41:40–41
Jacob blessed Pharaoh when he came before him, and again when he went out. Genesis 47:7 Genesis 47:10
Stephen: God "gave him favour and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh king of Egypt; and he made him governor over Egypt and all his house." Acts 7:10
The psalm: "The king sent and loosed him; even the ruler of the people, and let him go free." Psalms 105:20–21
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
Pharaoh spoke of Joseph as "a man in whom the Spirit of God is", because God had shown him the dreams' meaning. Genesis 41:38–39
Jacob blessed Pharaoh. Genesis 47:7 Genesis 47:10
Food was laid up "under the hand of Pharaoh" in the cities of Egypt. Genesis 41:35 Genesis 41:48
He invited Jacob's household into Egypt and gave them Goshen; Joseph's brothers could be made "rulers over my cattle". Genesis 45:17–20 Genesis 47:5–6
Joseph told his brothers to say they kept cattle, "for every shepherd is an abomination unto the Egyptians". Genesis 46:33–34
The Egyptians sold themselves and their land for bread: "we will be Pharaoh's servants". Genesis 47:19–25
EVENTS
Wars, works and turning points
UNDATED IN SCRIPTURE
DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
No name and no years. Any BC date depends on who he was; see the question below.
A Hyksos king
W. M. F. Petrie (1915); M. G. Kyle (1915); the Pulpit Commentary, naming Apophis; S. R. Driver (1911), on a late reckoning

Petrie takes Joseph's title "Bow the knee" (Abrekh) for a Babylonian title of the Hyksos period; Kyle reads the note that Potiphar was "an Egyptian" as a sign of a foreign court; the Pulpit Commentary supposes Joseph to have been "the minister of Apophis, the last Hyksos king". Driver adds that a 13th-century Exodus and 430 years would bring Jacob to Egypt "c. 1660–40 B.C., while the foreign kings, called the Hyksos, were ruling", though he calls the 430 years "very uncertain". Genesis 41:43 Genesis 39:1 [9][13][33][20]
A king of Manetho's list named by Ussher
James Ussher (1650–54), as reported by John Gill

Gill reports that Ussher, following Manetho's list, named the Pharaoh whose dreams Joseph interpreted Mephramuthosis, followed by Thmosis, Amenophis and Orus, in whose reign Joseph died. Exodus 1:8 [35]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture never gives this king's name.
Scripture does not say whether the Pharaoh who let Joseph bury Jacob (Gen 50:6) is the king who raised Joseph (Gen 41).
Scripture does not say when this king died; the next change it notes is "a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph", after Joseph and his generation had died (Exod 1:6, 8).
None of the records used for this page names Joseph or this king.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

From the textGenesis calls him only "Pharaoh" and "Pharaoh king of Egypt". This page follows the person record that gathers Genesis 37–50 under one king; Scripture does not say whether the Pharaoh who let Joseph bury Jacob is the king who raised him. Genesis 41:46 Genesis 50:6
